content: 1. Norelgestromin/ethinyl estradiol is applied as a transdermal patch. One patch is applied to the skin weekly for three weeks (on days 1, 8, and 15), followed by a patch-free week (days 22–28). This cycle is then repeated. 2. For initial treatment, the patch should be applied on the first day of menstruation (day 1). If applied after the first day, an additional form of contraception should be used for the next seven days. 3. When switching from oral contraceptives, the patch should be applied on the first day of withdrawal bleeding. If applied after the first day, an additional form of contraception is required for seven days. 4. After a first-trimester abortion, treatment can begin immediately. If not started within five days, an additional form of contraception should be used for seven days. 5. At the start of a new patch cycle, a new patch should be applied immediately and counted as day 1 of the cycle. An additional form of contraception is required for seven days. 6. If the patch is detached for less than 24 hours, it should be reapplied to the same location or replaced with a new patch immediately. If detached for more than 24 hours, a new patch should be applied immediately, and this is considered day 1 of a new cycle. Additional contraception is required for seven days. 7. If the patch is not used for more than one week, pregnancy should be ruled out before restarting treatment, and an additional form of contraception should be used for seven days. 8. Blood pressure should be monitored during use, and caution is advised. 9. At the end of the patch cycle (day 22), the patch should be removed immediately. The next patch should be applied at the usual start of the next cycle. 10. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Co-administration of ethinyl estradiol with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, including some >20x ULN). Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating these hepatitis C combination drugs and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 12. Co-administration of tranexamic acid and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 14. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the efficacy of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Anastrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 15. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 16. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 18.
